title: How would you estimate how many delivery pizzas the UK orders each week?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many delivery pizzas are ordered in the UK each week?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Here is a good first one to practise on. Read the question, pause, and have a go at your own estimate first, even a rough one. Then walk through the answer below and compare. Your number does not need to match; your logic is what counts.
body:
The question

How many delivery pizzas are ordered in the UK each week?

The approach

Households × share ordering this week × pizzas per order.

Say this out loud before you touch any numbers. It lets the interviewer agree with your plan, or nudge you, before you have done any work.

Step by step

  1. UK households: 28M
  2. × 15% order a delivery pizza in a typical week
  3. × 1.7 pizzas per order

That gives about 7.14M pizzas a week.

Does it make sense?

About 1 million a day, spread over a few thousand pizza takeaways.

This sanity check is the step most people skip, and one of the easiest ways to impress. It shows you care whether the number is right, not just whether the sum works.

Real-world check

UK households numbered about 28.6 million in 2024 (ONS), so 28 million is a sensible round number to start from.

Source: ONS: Families and households in the UK, 2024.

Your turn

Try a similar question in the free market sizing drill, which checks your logic step by step.
outro: If your estimate was far off, look for which step made the difference. That is where the learning is, and it is exactly what an interviewer would ask about.
